verdict.rationale: Kintsugi lets users create API keys with configurable expirations (never/1 month/6 months/1 year) and hold multiple keys simultaneously for rotation, giving some credential lifecycle control that could apply to an agent's key. However, there is no evidence of actual scope/permission restriction (e.g., read-only, endpoint-limited, or role-based keys) — every key appears to carry full account access via the same x-api-key/x-organization-id headers, and the MCP server explicitly avoids using API keys at all rather than issuing scoped ones. Missing for 10: granular permission/role-based scoping, agent-specific restricted keys, and any least-privilege access-control model beyond expiration.
